submitPageCreate (lines 2240-2300) — no generation capture, no isCurrent() call, unconditional tree write
handleRemoveSection (lines 1962-2096) — removeError's catch-write is ungated; the refetch immediately above IS gated with the same g
route-load reset callback — full range and cleared identifiers (lines 155-272)
findings.detail:
The reset callback is src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:155-272 (opens 'reset: ({ isSwitch }) => {' at line 155, closes '},' at line 272). It is passed as a property of the object literal given to createRouteLoadMachine({...}) which itself starts at line 149.

Unconditionally cleared (every load, not just isSwitch): reorderError (160), reorderStatus (161), reorderPending (167), removeError (173), pendingRemoveId (174), removePending (179), renamingSectionId (196), renameValue (197), renamePending (198), renameError (199), pendingDeactivateId (202), deactivateRefusal (203), deactivateActionError (204), deactivatePending (209), reinstatePending (215), inviteActionPending (226), recordEditorMemberId (240), recordEditorLookup (241), recordSaveError (242), recordStatus (248).

Cleared only under if (isSwitch) { ... } (256-271): showInactive (257), inactiveRows (258), inactiveLoadError (259), inviteLinkByMemberId (268), inviteErrorByMemberId (269), withdrawErrorByMemberId (270).

Deliberately NOT cleared here per inline comments (prior #287-era PO ruling, referenced at comment lines 190-195 and 231-236): renameStatus, removeStatus, pageCreateStatus. NOTE: issue #299's own comment thread (Gama, quoted in the issue) has since RULED that removeStatus and renameStatus should also be cleared going forward, and pageCreateStatus is explicitly targeted by #299's own done-when — but as of HEAD c89f2195 none of the three (renameStatus, removeStatus, pageCreateStatus) are actually present in the reset callback; the code has not yet caught up to that ruling.

Confirmed ABSENT from the reset callback entirely (grep across the whole file shows zero occurrences inside lines 155-272): sectionWriteError, pageCreateError, pageCreateStatus, pageCreateOpen, pageCreateName, pageCreateParentId. This is exactly what #299 claims as in-scope-but-missing — the fix needs to add clears for sectionWriteError, pageCreateError and pageCreateStatus (per #299's done-when bullet 3), plus a decision on pageCreateOpen/pageCreateName/pageCreateParentId (already ruled by Gama's comments on the issue: clear all three, with pageCreateParentId's clear needing a submit-time regression test, not just a state-reset test).

findings.title: Where each entry-level capture must go, and the after-an-await relocation trap
findings.detail:
handleCreate (2098-2164): capture must go before the FIRST await — immediately after the `if (!cfg) {...return;}` early-return block closes at line 2110, and before line 2123 (`newId = await createSection(cfg, {...input, dbEntityId})`). Concretely: insert `const g = routeLoad.generation;` right after line 2110. Then guard every settle-time write after each await: after the createSection await (2123), guard the tree mutation at 2148 (and the expandedIds write at 2152); after the assignMemberSection await (2155), guard patchMemberSectionIds at 2163; and guard the two catch-block sectionWriteError writes at 2126 and 2160. Trap check: there is currently NO existing generation/isCurrent token anywhere in this function (confirmed by grep — zero matches across lines 2098-2164), so there is no existing capture sitting after a bumping await to relocate; the fix is a fresh insertion, not a relocation, so the classic trap (capturing generation after an await that already bumped it) does not apply here — but the builder must still take care to place the NEW capture before the *first* await (2123), not merely before the tree-mutation line (2148), since assignMemberSection's own catch branch (2156-2161) also needs the same g.

submitPageCreate (2240-2300): capture must go before the ONLY await — after the `if (!cfg) {...return;}` guard closes at line 2268, and before line 2272 (`newId = await createSection(cfg, {...})`). Concretely: insert `const g = routeLoad.generation;` right after line 2268. Guard the settle-time writes at 2296 (tree mutation), 2297 (expandedIds), 2298 (pageCreateStatus), 2299 (closePageCreateForm(), which writes pageCreateOpen/pageCreateName/pageCreateParentId/pageCreateError), and the catch-block pageCreateError write at 2275. Trap check: same as handleCreate — zero existing generation tokens in this function, so this is a fresh insertion with no relocation trap.

handleRemoveSection (1962-2096): a capture ALREADY EXISTS — const g = routeLoad.generation; at line 2007, which sits correctly BEFORE the function's only structural await (await deleteSection(cfg, id) at line 2021) and before the nested await listSections(cfg) retry (2072). This existing capture point is correctly placed (before the first await, not after) and the trap (an existing capture sitting after an await that already bumped the generation) does NOT apply to it — it is already reused correctly by the refetch-reconcile guards at 2073/2077 and the removePending clear at 2093. The actual gap here (finding 3) needs no new capture at all: it needs two more guard sites reusing the SAME already-in-scope g — one before the removeError/failedRemoveId writes at 2083-2084 (e.g. `if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;` placed just before 2083, though care is needed since pendingRemoveId's 'stay armed for retry' contract at the comment on 2085 must still hold for the non-stale case), and one guarding the finally block's placeFocusAfterFailedRemove call at line 2094 (currently only the removePending clear at 2093 is guarded; the focus-placement call right beside it is not).

findings.title: Confirmed instance #1 (the seeded one): roster new-section parent select
findings.detail: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte. Variable `pageCreateParentId` (declared ~2183). Options come from `ownOrgFlatSections` (`$derived(flattenSections(visibleSections))`), which is collective-scoped and rebuilt on every load. `pageCreateParentId` is reset to '' only in `openPageCreateForm`/`closePageCreateForm` (~2220/2228) — it is NOT touched by the route-load machine's `reset:` callback (verified by reading the whole callback body, which resets ~15 other transient fields but never this one, nor `pageCreateOpen`/`pageCreateName`). If the create-section form is left open across a collective switch, the `<select>` (value={pageCreateParentId}, onchange writes back to it) displays its first real option ("top level") because none of the new collective's `ownOrgFlatSections` match the old id, while the variable still holds the old collective's section id. `submitPageCreate` reads `pageCreateParentId` directly and calls `createSection(cfg, { parentId, dbEntityId: currentDbEntityId })` against the NEW collective's cfg with the OLD collective's parent id — this is exactly the issue #299 scope description, verified independently by reading the reset function and the submit path.

findings.title: Confirmed second instance: library bulk-checkout work/edition selects (display divergence reachable, write blocked by an unrelated invariant)
findings.detail: src/routes/library/+page.svelte, lines ~181-184 (state), ~313-319 (`reset:` callback), ~1089-1102 (the two `<select>`s), ~1038-1071 (`handleBulkCheckout`). `bulkCheckoutWorkId`/`bulkCheckoutEditionId`/`bulkCheckoutCheckedMembers`/`bulkCheckoutDueDate` are plain page-level `$state`, never gated behind an open/close form (the picker is always mounted whenever `$librarianStore === 'librarian'`). Options come from `works`/`filteredBulkCheckoutEditions`, both derived from collective-scoped data (`listWorks(cfg)` in the route-load machine's `load()`). The `reset:` callback (called on every load, switch or refresh) clears five unrelated caches but never `bulkCheckoutWorkId`/`bulkCheckoutEditionId`/`bulkCheckoutCheckedMembers`/`bulkCheckoutDueDate`; `onNoCollective` only clears `works=[]`. An `$effect` clears `bulkCheckoutEditionId` when `bulkCheckoutWorkId` CHANGES (line ~780) but never refires if the id value itself is unchanged across a switch (Svelte effects rerun on value change, not on unrelated data reload) — so a stale edition id from the previous collective can also survive. Reachable sequence: librarian in collective A picks Work X (Edition Y); switches to collective B where they are also a librarian; `works`/`allEditions`/`allCopies` reload to B's data; the work `<select>` silently falls back to its placeholder option in the DOM (X's id matches nothing in B) while `bulkCheckoutWorkId` still equals X — a genuine, reachable display/value divergence of exactly the #299 shape. However, `handleBulkCheckout` (the submit path, which DOES read `bulkCheckoutEditionId` directly) is gated by a disabled attribute on the submit button keyed off `bulkCheckoutCheckedMembers.size > bulkCheckoutEditionAvailability.available`, and `deriveEditionAvailability(staleEditionId, allCopies-of-B, ...)` always returns `{available: 0, total: 0}` for a foreign edition id absent from B's copies — so any nonzero checked-member count exceeds 0 and the button stays disabled. `handleBulkCheckout` itself has no independent guard against a stale/foreign edition id, so this safety is accidental (a side effect of availability arithmetic, not a deliberate switch-guard) and would break if that arithmetic or the disabled condition ever changed. Net: the display bug is real and reachable; the destructive cross-collective write it was feared to enable is not reachable through the UI today, unlike the roster instance where the wrong-tree write goes through uncontested.

findings.title: Negative — every other dynamic-option <select> checked and found NOT vulnerable
findings.detail: Swept every `<select>`/`bind:value`/`value={...}` site under src/routes/**/+page.svelte and src/lib/components/** (10 files with `<select>`; also checked role="radio"/"radiogroup" groups). Findings, all verified by reading the surrounding reset/close/effect code: (1) admin/+page.svelte's admin/librarian-add pickers (~652,734) and every `#209 PO-rule-1` "prompt" picker across the app (season-manage-conductor-select, season-create's conductor picker, event-create's conductor picker, admin's two pickers) always render `value=""` and the `onchange` handler resets the DOM element to `''` synchronously before consuming the pick — there is no persisted variable holding a stale selection, so the defect shape cannot occur by construction. (2) src/routes/+page.svelte's `eventCreateSeasonId`/`eventCreateSeriesId` (season/series pickers) ARE cleared synchronously and unconditionally by `closeEventCreateForm()`, which `loadForSelected()` calls on every load (both the no-collective branch and the real-selection branch) before any async work starts — confirmed by reading `closeEventCreateForm`'s full body and its two call sites in `loadForSelected`. `seasonCreateConductors`/`eventCreate*` chip arrays are likewise fully cleared by `closeSeasonCreateForm`. `eventCreateType`/`seriesCreateType`/`seriesCreateRepeat`/`seriesCreateDay` and the event-type/location selects on the event detail page and event-create/edit forms all draw from fixed, non-collective-scoped lists (CANONICAL_EVENT_TYPES, repeat patterns, day-of-week, TimeSelect's generated hour/minute lists) so there is no reloadable option set for the value to diverge from. (3) The season-manage panel's `<RepertoireElement>` (selectedWorkId/selectedEditionForAdd) is unmounted outright on a genuine switch — `resetSeasonManage()` sets `seasonManageOpen = false`, and it is called (with `dropConvertRun: true`) from both branches of `loadForSelected` before the async load starts; the component's internal `$state` is destroyed with it. The per-event `<RepertoireElement>` instances inside AgendaList are inside `{#each ... as item (item.id)}` keyed by event id (an Entu ObjectId, globally unique — confirmed via entu-www docs, `db-mutations/index.md:78`), so a collective switch replaces the item list with disjoint ids and Svelte destroys/recreates every instance, resetting internal picker state by construction. (4) `SectionPicker.svelte`'s inline "+ New section" parent-select (`createParentId`) is likewise inside a `{#each rows as row (row.memberId)}` keyed block in roster/+page.svelte; member ids are Entu ObjectIds scoped per-database, so a switch cannot preserve a matching key across collectives and the component (with its internal `createParentId`) is destroyed and recreated. (5) InviteSurface.svelte's `dbId` picker is the account's own cross-collective membership list (`availableDbs`, not per-collective reloadable data — this select IS how the operator chooses/changes the collective, not something that reloads AS A RESULT of switching), and its `$effect`s already fail closed to `''`/`'no-collective'` whenever the list empties; the shape does not match "collective-scoped options reloaded out from under a persisted selection." (6) profile/+page.svelte's two selects (time-format, roster-real-names) both have a fully static 2-option set never affected by any collective's data. (7) library/+page.svelte's inline per-copy checkout select and admin's two role/librarian selects use the same self-resetting `value=""` pattern as (1). (8) All `role="radio"`/`role="radiogroup"` controls found (roster view-mode chips, library copy-sort chips) enumerate fixed, non-data-derived option sets. No other instance of the synchronous defect class was found.

findings.title: All three handler-start clears confirmed at current line numbers; no bypass path exists
findings.detail:
Each of the three vars has exactly one clear site and exactly one write site in the whole file (verified by exhaustive grep — no other occurrences exist):
- `removeStatus`: declared `src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1951`; cleared at `handleRemoveSection` line 1995 (second statement in the function, right after `removeError = null` at 1992, before the `structuralWritePending`/`!cfg` bail-outs and the `deleteSection` await); the only write is the success branch at line 2055.
- `pageCreateStatus`: declared line 2193; cleared at `submitPageCreate` line 2244 (second statement, right after `pageCreateError = null` at 2243, before the empty-name/duplicate/`!cfg` bail-outs and the `createSection` await); only write is success branch at line 2298.
- `renameStatus`: declared line 2777; cleared at `startRename` line 2800 (second statement, after the `structuralWritePending` early-return guard at 2798, which fires before setting `renamingSectionId` and thus before `submitRename` can ever run); only write is success branch in `submitRename` at line 2845.
`submitRename`'s own bail-outs (`id === null`, blank name, `structuralWritePending`, `!cfg`) all `return` before reaching the write at 2845, and `submitRename` is only reachable at all after `startRename` has already run (it is the sole writer of `renamingSectionId`, which `submitRename` gates on at line 2815). So there is no code path — early return, catch branch, or otherwise — that reaches a status write without first passing its own function's clear statement. The task's 'no missed-announcement bug' premise holds.

findings.title: Residual: stale cross-collective sentence sits in the DOM, sr-only but reachable by a linear-reading screen-reader pass, never visible to sighted users
findings.detail: All three live regions (`roster-section-remove-status` line 4148-4155, `roster-section-create-status` 4161-4168, `roster-section-rename-status` 4173-4180) are `role="status" aria-live="polite" class="sr-only"`, mounted unconditionally at the top of the template — before the `{#if status === 'no-collective'}` branch at line 4195 — so they render on every page state (loading, no-collective, load-error, populated) regardless of which collective is selected. `sr-only` hides the text only visually (clip/absolute-position technique); it does NOT remove the node from the accessibility tree. So: (1) visually, the residual is never exposed — sighted users can never see it, in any state, ever (confirmed: sr-only is unconditional, not gated on any status flag). (2) For assistive tech, the aria-live mechanism only fires on a mutation, so an unchanged stale string is never re-announced spontaneously — no phantom announcement on switch. But a screen-reader user who linearly browses the page (virtual-cursor arrow navigation, 'read all', or simply tabbing/reading through top-of-page content) WILL land on this DOM text node and have it read aloud, since it is ordinary AT-visible text, just CSS-hidden from sighted view. If collective A's rename produced 'Tenor section renamed' and the user then switches to collective B without performing a matching action there, that sentence remains live in the DOM, misattributed to a screen on which it never happened, until the user performs the corresponding action in B (which clears-then-writes, per finding 1). This is a real but narrow residual: no sighted-visual leak, no spurious live-region announcement, but a genuine stale-content exposure to AT users who browse rather than merely listen for changes.

findings.title: #287-era reasoning for excluding the three status vars from reset, and the #268-era identical-string hazard comment
findings.detail:
#287-era reasoning (inside the `reset` callback): line 190-195 — "`renameStatus` is deliberately NOT included here — see the #287-era comment below, which this keeps following rather than overturning: it is an 'invisible success' announcement naming a past action by value, not by on-screen tree position, so a switch does not make it wrong the way `reorderStatus`'s position-describing text would be." And the fuller three-way statement at lines 227-236: "...unconditionally on EVERY load, not just an actual switch (matching `reorderStatus` above and `recordStatus` below — `removeStatus`/`pageCreateStatus`/`renameStatus` are NOT cleared here, per #287 review, a decision #297 read and kept for `renameStatus` rather than overturning; the rename trio's other four vars (`renamingSectionId`/`renameValue`/`renamePending`/`renameError`) ARE cleared, alongside `removePending`, above)..."

#268-era identical-string hazard comment: `saveRecordEditor`, lines 1641-1649 — "#268 review — a fresh attempt owns the live region too, same discipline as `armedRemove`/`submitPageCreate`/`startRename` above. Two things break without it: (1) a SECOND consecutive success reassigns the identical string, the DOM text never changes, and `aria-live="polite"` announces nothing; (2) a save that FAILS would leave the previous 'Member details saved.' sitting in the status region beside the role="alert" that says nothing was saved — the #253 lying-banner class, in the accessibility tree. Cleared BEFORE the required-name gate below so a refusal clears it too." This comment is the canonical statement of why each handler clears its own status at entry (same-collective repeat-success and repeat-failure hazards), and it explicitly names `startRename`/`submitPageCreate`/`armedRemove` as sharing this discipline — confirming the handler-start clears in the three vars under review exist for this reason, distinct from (and unrelated to) the cross-collective residual in finding 2.

findings.title: Recommendation: leave as-is — do not add the three status vars to reset's unconditional clear
findings.detail:
Arguments for clearing on switch: it would eliminate the residual in finding 2 outright — no stale cross-collective sentence could ever sit in the DOM, closing even the narrow linear-AT-browsing exposure; it would also make the three vars' reset treatment uniform with `reorderStatus`/`recordStatus`, reducing the 'why are these three different' cognitive load for future maintainers reading `reset`.

Arguments for leaving as-is: (a) this is a deliberate, twice-reaffirmed decision — #287 made it, #297 explicitly re-read it for `renameStatus` and chose to keep it rather than overturn it, so a third pass changing it needs a new, distinct reason, not a rediscovery of the same tradeoff. (b) The stated rationale still holds under inspection: these three announce "a past action, by value" (e.g. "Tenor section renamed") rather than `reorderStatus`'s on-screen-position-describing text, so a switch does not make the sentence factually WRONG the way a stale position claim would be — it's merely stale, not false. (c) The actual exposure surface is narrow and now precisely characterized (finding 2): zero visual leak, zero spurious `aria-live` announcement, and even the AT-linear-browsing case self-heals the instant the user performs the corresponding action on the new collective, because the handler-start clear (finding 1) guarantees a fresh empty-then-text cycle every time. (d) Adding a clear here is not free: it enlarges `reset`'s already-large unconditional-clear surface and reintroduces exactly the kind of no-real-bug 'symmetry cleanup' that #297 already looked at and rejected for `renameStatus` specifically.

Recommendation: leave as-is. The residual is real but cosmetic-to-AT-only, self-heals on next action, and reopening a twice-settled decision without new evidence of actual harm (a repro of a user being misled, not just an asymmetry) is not warranted. If this is added to #299, frame it as a documented, low-severity, already-triaged residual rather than a defect requiring a code change.

findings.title: Abort check passed — correct repo confirmed
findings.detail: `git remote get-url origin` in ~/workspace-app returns https://github.com/mvox-dev/mvox-app.git — ends in mvox-app.git, so the investigation proceeded per the task's own gate. ~/workspace (sibling) was not read.

findings.title: #298's two named regions: exact markup, testid, variable, classes
findings.detail:
Both live in src/routes/+page.svelte, both always-mounted (no {#if} wrapper), both `role="status" aria-live="polite" class="sr-only"`, no other classes. `season-create-status` — line 7222: `
{seasonCreateStatus}
`. `event-create-status` — line 7389, same shape, renders `{eventCreateStatus}`. `seasonCreateStatus`/`eventCreateStatus` are `$state('')` (declared line 2239 / 3304), set to the localized success string on a successful write (line 2437 `m.season_created({name})`; line 4547 `m.event_created({name, when})`) and reset to `''` at various points (see next finding for gaps in that reset coverage).

findings.title: Roster's sibling sr-only regions are a SEPARATE concern, not in #298's scope
findings.detail: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte has five of its own always-mounted sr-only role="status" regions built on the identical idiom: `roster-reorder-status` (4117), `roster-section-remove-status` (4148-4155), `roster-section-create-status` (4161-4168), `roster-section-rename-status` (4173-4180), `roster-member-record-status` (4186-4193). #298's body and Done-when checklist name only `event-create-status` and `season-create-status`; none of the roster testids appear anywhere in the issue text. A sixth clone of the same pattern lives outside both named files too: src/routes/+page.svelte's own `season-manage-delete-status` (line 7210-7217, same page, also not named in #298) and a /profile page confirmation region referenced in src/routes/page.profile-repair-confirmation.spec.ts:16-23 ("exactly like `event-create-status` ... and `roster-reorder-status`"). So the pattern is used in at least 8 places across the app; #298 as filed scopes exactly 2 of them. The roster siblings/season-manage-delete-status are a later-generalization question, explicitly deferred by #298's own "Not scoped" section ("Whether this region generalises beyond create is a later question").

findings.title: sr-only mechanism is Tailwind v4's stock utility; no custom override
findings.detail: No `.sr-only` rule exists anywhere under source (grepped app.css / no tailwind.config with a sr-only override) — package.json pins `tailwindcss ^4.3.3`/`@tailwindcss/vite ^4.3.3`, and the compiled CSS shows Tailwind's stock definition: `.sr-only{clip-path:inset(50%);white-space:nowrap;border-width:0;width:1px;height:1px;margin:-1px;padding:0;position:absolute;overflow:hidden}`. Position:absolute means the element is already out of flow today — it currently occupies zero layout space regardless of content.

findings.title: No precedent in either file for ANY dynamic class binding — content-presence-conditional visibility would be the first instance of this pattern
findings.detail: grep for `class:` (Svelte's class-directive shorthand) and for `class={` (a dynamic/computed class attribute of any kind) returns zero hits in both src/routes/+page.svelte and src/routes/roster/+page.svelte. Every class attribute in both files is a static string literal. So there is no existing precedent for a conditionally-visible-but-always-present element via ANY mechanism (CSS :empty, a Svelte class: directive, or a ternary class expression) — #298's fix would introduce the first dynamic-class binding in either file. The closest thing that exists is the OPPOSITE, forbidden shape: `series-create-progress` (line 6719) and `event-convert-progress` (lines 7088-7100) are visible `role="status" aria-live="polite"` paragraphs mounted via `{#if progressVar}` — i.e. exactly the "conditionally MOUNTED" anti-pattern #298's issue body calls out by name ("visibility must come from styling on content presence, never an {#if} around the region"). These are not usable as a model for #298; if anything they are the pattern to avoid.

findings.title: The simplest correct implementation is a plain Svelte reactive class expression, not a CSS :empty selector — and :empty has a real pitfall here
findings.detail:
Because Svelte 5 already re-renders `{seasonCreateStatus}`/`{eventCreateStatus}` reactively, a `class={status ? '' : 'sr-only'}` (or `class:sr-only={!status}`) driven off the SAME state var the text already binds to is a direct, low-risk way to satisfy "visibility from content presence" without introducing a CSS :empty dependency at all — it keeps the element permanently mounted (satisfying the hard constraint) and needs no new selector mechanics. [speculative: this is the natural fix shape, not something confirmed against a plan/PR] — By contrast, a CSS `:empty`/Tailwind `empty:` approach is riskier than it looks: the compiled Svelte template for these divs is `
` (a literal single-space text-node placeholder — confirmed via .svelte-kit/output/client/_app/immutable/nodes/2.3P-ipHGL.js, grep for `season-create-status`), and Svelte's reactive text-set (`set_text`) mutates that text node's `.data` rather than removing the node. Whether a *zero-length* text-node child still counts as a child for `:empty` matching is genuinely ambiguous per the CSS spec text itself (MDN: "Children can be either element nodes or text (including whitespace)" — does not disambiguate zero-length strings), and I could not empirically verify browser behavior in this environment (claude-in-chrome's extension is not connected here; a local happy-dom probe gave an internally-inconsistent result — it reported `:empty` matching even with non-empty textContent — so happy-dom is not trustworthy evidence either way, and no Chromium binary is cached locally for a real Playwright run). Recommend the plain reactive-class approach specifically because it sidesteps this unverified edge case entirely.

findings.title: Surrounding layout: the two regions sit in a non-flex, non-gapped block container — a newly-visible line would need its own spacing
findings.detail: Both `season-create-status` and `event-create-status` (and `season-manage-delete-status` between them) are direct children of `<div class="rounded-lg bg-paper p-4">` (opened at src/routes/+page.svelte:5705) — confirmed by bracket-depth-walking the div nesting from line 7210 back to the nearest unclosed `<div>`. That container has NO `flex`/`gap` class; its children rely on their own margin utilities for spacing (e.g. the season-create-form block below carries `mb-3`). Since the regions are currently `position:absolute` (sr-only), they take zero space today regardless. If made visible without adding a margin utility, the new visible line would sit flush against whatever renders immediately before/after it in source order (season-manage-delete-status above, the season-create-form/trigger below) — worth a deliberate spacing decision, not automatic. NOTE for contrast: roster/+page.svelte's five equivalent regions (out of #298's scope) DO sit inside a `flex flex-col gap-4` container (`<div class="mx-auto flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-4">`, roster/+page.svelte:4109) — so spacing there would be automatic if that page were ever touched; +page.svelte's container is not analogous.

findings.title: Existing specs assert role/aria-live/textContent — none assert `sr-only`-ness, and season-create-status has ZERO test coverage today
findings.detail: Three spec files assert on `event-create-status` (src/routes/page.event-create.spec.ts:1390-1501,1838; src/routes/page.event-create-collapse.spec.ts — comment-only cross-reference at line 36; src/routes/page.profile-repair-confirmation.spec.ts — comment-only cross-reference at line 18/234). The live assertions in page.event-create.spec.ts check `getAttribute('role')==='status'`, `getAttribute('aria-live')==='polite'`, and `.textContent?.trim()` (empty at mount, populated after a successful write, empty again on failure) — none of them check `class`/`sr-only`/computed visibility. So a visibility-styling change (toggling the class) will NOT break any of these assertions as written today. Separately: `grep -rn 'season-create-status'` across the whole repo (excluding node_modules/.svelte-kit/build) finds it ONLY in src/routes/+page.svelte itself and in three memory/research JSON files under teams/mvox-dev/ — there is no spec file anywhere asserting on `season-create-status` at all today. This matches #298's Done-when item 3 ("A test asserts the announcement still fires") reading as new coverage to be WRITTEN for season-create, not an existing guard to preserve.

findings.title: Verified gap vs. #298's own Done-when clearing rule: neither status var clears on form reopen (event) or on any context change (both)
findings.detail: #298 Done-when: "The message clears on the next create, on form reopen, or on a context change — no timer." At HEAD: (a) `openSeasonCreateForm` (src/routes/+page.svelte:2271) DOES clear `seasonCreateStatus = ''` on reopen. (b) `openEventCreateForm` (src/routes/+page.svelte:3355-3389) does NOT reset `eventCreateStatus` anywhere in its body — it resets every other form field but not the status var; `eventCreateStatus` is cleared only inside `submitEventCreate` (line 4427), i.e. only at next-create time, not at reopen. (c) Neither `closeSeasonCreateForm` (2291-2298) nor `closeEventCreateForm` (3405-3423) clears its respective status var. (d) `loadForSelected`'s no-collective/deselect branch (src/routes/+page.svelte:638-687) calls both close-functions and resets a long list of other state, but neither `seasonCreateStatus` nor `eventCreateStatus` appears anywhere in that function body (grepped the full function) — a genuine collective switch does not clear either status today. This is currently invisible/harmless because both regions are sr-only (a screen-reader user who already left the page context won't hear a stale announcement fire again on its own — the live region only announces on a CHANGE). It becomes user-visible and behaviorally wrong the moment #298 makes the region visible: a stale "Season X created" line could sit on screen after switching collectives or reopening the event form without creating anything. This gap needs to be closed as part of the fix, not assumed already handled.

findings.title: i18n: existing copy is reused verbatim for the base case; the #244 excluded-by-filter case (Done-when item 6) has NO existing message key
findings.detail: `season_created` ("{name} created.") and `event_created` ("{name} created for {when}.") in messages/en.json:426,497 are plain, display-appropriate sentences already used for the sr-only announcement — no rewording needed to show them visually. However #298's Done-when item 6 ("#244's excluded-by-filter case has somewhere to say so: created successfully, and the active filter is why it is not in the list") maps to a real code branch with no matching copy today: `submitEventCreate` (src/routes/+page.svelte:4547-4591) sets `eventCreateStatus` to the plain `event_created` message BEFORE computing `showableUnderFilter` (line 4587-4591, used only to decide whether to call `surfaceCreatedEvent`) — the status text itself never varies by filter outcome. `grep -rn 'excluded\|filtered_out\|hidden_by_filter'` across +page.svelte and messages/ finds nothing. So this Done-when item needs a genuinely NEW message key (four-bundle: en/et/lv/uk, per the project's i18n convention referenced in src/routes/page.event-create-collapse.spec.ts:38-40) — it is not a case of reusing existing copy.

findings.title: Double-announcement risk is real only if the fix adds a NEW element instead of restyling the existing one — issue text already anticipates this
findings.detail: Toggling the SAME element's class (visible text and the live-region role on one node) is safe: it produces exactly one announcement channel (the live region) and one visual presentation, not two. The real double-announce risk is procedural, not stylistic: if an implementer instead reaches for the codebase's OTHER existing visible-status idiom — the `{#if}`-mounted `role="status"` paragraphs like `event-convert-progress` (src/routes/+page.svelte:7088-7100) or `series-create-progress` (6719) — and adds a NEW such paragraph alongside leaving the existing sr-only `event-create-status`/`season-create-status` untouched, a screen-reader user would get the success text announced once by the untouched live region and then encounter it again as ordinary static content when navigating the page — a real double-exposure (not necessarily a double aria-live announcement, but a duplicated read). The issue body itself preempts exactly this by insisting "No toast, no component... Reuse what is there" (gh issue view 298 body) — so this risk is a matter of following the issue's own explicit instruction, confirmed consistent with everything found above.
